sights.address: Ukrainian Village, Chicago, IL 60622 (street number pending re-verify)
sights.w: 1915 Neo-Byzantine cathedral modelled on Kyiv's St. Sophia — its thirteen copper domes crown Ukrainian Village; interior mosaics are among Chicago's finest.

sights.address: Logan Blvd, Kedzie Blvd & Palmer Sq around Logan Square, Chicago, IL 60647
sights.w: The Northwest Side's grandest stretch of Chicago's boulevard system — graystone 'boulevard of the millionaires' mansions around Logan and Palmer squares (NRHP + Chicago Landmark district).

sights.n: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts and Culture
sights.address: Humboldt Park (1895 park stables), Chicago, IL 60622
sights.w: The only US national museum devoted to Puerto Rican art, in Humboldt Park's 1895 stables — the park's oldest building.

sights.address: Milwaukee / North / Damen six-way intersection, Wicker Park, Chicago
sights.w: The triangular 1929 Art Deco Northwest Tower — first skyscraper of its size outside downtown — at the six-way Milwaukee/North/Damen crossing, now a hotel with skyline rooftop bars.

sights.address: 1327 N Noble St, Chicago, IL 60642
sights.w: Mother church of Chicago Polonia (1867–81, Patrick Keely) — by 1897 the largest parish in the US; a 'Polish Cathedral' landmark in Noble Square.

sights.address: Pierce Ave & Hoyne Ave around Wicker Park, Chicago, IL 60622
sights.w: Victorian mansions of 'Beer Baron Row' (Hoyne) and Pierce Ave lining the 1870 park — one of the city's best post-Fire residential streetscapes (Chicago Landmark district).

sights.address: Alta Vista Terrace, Lakeview (Wrigleyville), Chicago, IL 60613
sights.w: 'Street of Forty Doors' — a single block of London-style rowhouses (1900–04) mirrored end to end; Chicago's first designated historic district (1971), steps from Wrigley Field.

sights.address: W Argyle St, Uptown, Chicago, IL 60640
sights.w: Where Charlie Chaplin made 'His New Job' and Gloria Swanson started out — the 1907 silent-film studio's terracotta-trimmed home, a Chicago Landmark (now St. Augustine College).

sights.address: 503 W Wrightwood Ave, Chicago, IL 60614
sights.w: Brewer Francis Dewes's 1896 Lincoln Park mansion — exuberant German Baroque, with caryatids holding up the balcony; a Chicago Landmark beside his brother's matching house.

sights.address: 5255 N Pulaski Rd, Chicago, IL 60630
sights.w: Freethinkers' cemetery founded 1877 by Czech immigrants — Bohemian-art monuments, Mayor Anton Cermak's grave and the Eastland-disaster victims; CAC-toured.

sights.address: Village of Riverside, IL 60546
sights.w: Olmsted & Vaux's 1869 curving-street suburb along the Des Plaines River — one of America's first planned communities, a National Historic Landmark (expanded 2023).

sights.address: Riverside, IL 60546 (private residence)
sights.w: Wright's own 'most successful of my houses' (1906–09) — a long, low U-shaped Prairie complex set into Olmsted's Riverside; National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

sights.n: Ward W. Willits House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
sights.address: 1445 Sheridan Rd, Highland Park, IL 60035
sights.w: Widely considered Wright's first mature Prairie-style house (1901–02), on Highland Park's Sheridan Road — a National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

sights.address: 1200 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
sights.w: 1930 Beaux-Arts aquarium on Museum Campus — 32,000 animals, beluga whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins in the lake-view Abbott Oceanarium.

sights.address: N Michigan Ave between Randolph St and Monroe St, Chicago, IL 60602
sights.w: The 24.5-acre front lawn of Chicago (2004) — Cloud Gate, Crown Fountain, Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the hidden Lurie Garden, with free summer concerts.

sights.address: E Erie St, River North, Chicago (Nickerson Mansion)
sights.w: The 1883 Nickerson 'Marble Palace' — marble floors, grand staircases and Gilded Age decorative arts, a block off Michigan Avenue.

sights.address: S Wentworth Ave, Chinatown, Chicago, IL 60616
sights.w: The 1928 On Leong Merchants Association building — pagoda towers, green tile roofs and terracotta, Chinatown's signature landmark (Chicago Landmark 1993).

sights.address: S Wabash Ave, Bronzeville (Near South Side), Chicago
sights.w: Home of Chicago's oldest Black congregation (1844), an Underground Railroad station; its 1892 sanctuary still stands at Bronzeville's northern edge (Chicago Landmark).

sights.address: Bronzeville, Chicago, IL 60653
sights.w: Birthplace of gospel music — Thomas A. Dorsey's 1931 choir here launched Mahalia Jackson and a new American sound (Chicago Landmark 2011).

sights.n: Site of the Great Chicago Fire (Pillar of Fire)
sights.address: 558 W DeKoven St, Chicago, IL 60607
sights.w: Where the 1871 fire began in the O'Leary barn — now, fittingly, the CFD's Quinn Fire Academy, with Egon Weiner's bronze 'Pillar of Fire' and a plaque marking the spot (Chicago Landmark).

sights.address: Lakefront from North Ave to Ardmore Ave, Chicago (Chicago Park District)
sights.w: Chicago's largest park (1868) — seven miles of lakefront with the free zoo, conservatory, North Pond, Caldwell Lily Pool, beaches and the Lakefront Trail.

sights.address: N Clark St around Foster & Balmoral Aves, Andersonville, Chicago
sights.w: The old Swedish village on Clark Street — indie shops, Swedish bakeries and the flag-painted water tower; Time Out once voted it the coolest neighbourhood in the US (NRHP district).

sights.address: N Sheridan Rd at the north end of Lake Shore Drive, Edgewater, Chicago
sights.w: The pink 1928 tower at the end of Lake Shore Drive — the surviving sister of the vanished Edgewater Beach Hotel resort (NRHP).

sights.address: 900–1100 blocks of W Bryn Mawr Ave (Sheridan Rd to Broadway), Edgewater, Chicago
sights.w: Three blocks of 1897–1928 apartment hotels and terracotta façades once home to Chicago's elite — Bryn Mawr & Belle Shore hotels; made a Chicago Landmark district in Sept 2026.

sights.address: 10244 S Longwood Dr, Chicago, IL 60643
sights.w: An 1886 limestone 'Irish castle' on the Beverly ridge, built by developer Robert Givins for his bride — home of Beverly Unitarian Church since 1941.

sights.address: 9801 S Avenue G, Chicago, IL 60617
sights.w: 181-acre East Side lakefront park with a sandy beach, a 1924 Classical Revival fieldhouse (Chicago Landmark) and a model-train exhibit; views to the Indiana steel shore.

sights.address: 700 W Adams St, Chicago, IL 60661
sights.w: Chicago's oldest public building (1856) and a Great Fire survivor — Celtic-revival windows and Book of Kells-inspired stencils in the West Loop.

sights.address: S Dearborn St at W Adams St, the Loop, Chicago
sights.w: Holabird & Roche's 1895 Chicago School landmark — Tiffany mosaics of Père Marquette's voyage and Edward Kemeys bronzes in the lobby.

sights.address: N Michigan Ave, the Loop, Chicago (Pendry Chicago hotel)
sights.w: The Burnham brothers' 1929 black-granite and gold-leaf Art Deco tower — said to be modelled on a champagne bottle — now the Pendry hotel with a rooftop bar.

sights.address: 1827 S Indiana Ave, Chicago, IL 60616
sights.w: Chicago's oldest house (1836), the Greek Revival home of Henry & Caroline Clarke, now a city-run museum in the Prairie Avenue district.

sights.address: 111 E Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60601
sights.w: The city's architecture HQ on the river — supersized skyscraper models, the lit-up downtown model, and the departure dock for its famous 90-minute First Lady river cruise.

sights.address: S Michigan Ave, Prairie Avenue district, Chicago
sights.w: Gothic Revival church re-done inside in Arts & Crafts style by Howard Van Doren Shaw after a 1900 fire — 21 stained-glass windows, nine by Tiffany (NHL).

sights.address: W Washington St, the Loop, Chicago
sights.w: The 1924 First United Methodist 'Chicago Temple' — the world's tallest church building, with a tiny Sky Chapel in its spire 400 ft above the Loop.

sights.address: Irving Park — blocks around Avers & Hamlin Aves north of Addison St, Chicago
sights.w: Seven boulevard blocks of 126 Prairie & Craftsman bungalows (1907–25) with double lots and deep setbacks — a hidden NRHP + Chicago Landmark district.

sights.address: 5216 W Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL 60630
sights.w: Rapp & Rapp's 1930 Gateway movie palace, restored as the Polish-American Copernicus cultural centre — concerts and dance most nights; next door to the Taste of Polonia festival.

sights.address: 756 N Milwaukee Ave, Chicago, IL 60642
sights.w: America's leading museum of outsider and self-taught art — home of the recreated Henry Darger Room; reopened in 2025 after a major expansion.

sights.address: Ukrainian Village, Chicago (Chicago Landmark district)
sights.w: Chicago Landmark district of worker cottages and two-flats around the onion-domed churches — the heart of the city's Ukrainian community (CAC walking tour).

sights.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Historic District (Oak Park)
sights.address: Oak Park, IL 60302 (historic district)
sights.w: The world's largest concentration of Wright buildings — two dozen Prairie houses within walking distance of his Home & Studio; FLW Trust guided walks April–November.
sights.k: frank lloyd wright architecture historic district

sights.address: 40 Arts Circle Dr, Evanston, IL 60208
sights.w: Northwestern's free art museum on the lakefill campus — prints, photography, film and ambitious exhibitions.

sights.address: 615 Garfield St, Oak Park, IL 60304
sights.w: 1929 glasshouse with 20,000 plants in Mediterranean, tropical and desert rooms — a free hidden gem south of downtown Oak Park.

sights.address: W Jackson Blvd between Laflin St and Ashland Ave, Near West Side, Chicago
sights.w: A block of 1880s Victorian rowhouses and mansions that survived the West Side's decline — a Chicago Landmark district and NRHP listing.

sights.address: 5610 W Lake St, Chicago, IL 60644
sights.w: 1929 town hall at the heart of Austin — now a Chicago Park District cultural centre and fieldhouse with a historic auditorium.

sights.address: W Argyle St between Broadway and Sheridan Rd, Uptown, Chicago
sights.w: Chicago's 'Little Saigon' — a few blocks of pho houses, bakeries and Asian markets around the Argyle 'L' stop (NRHP historic district; Asia on Argyle night market).

sights.address: 11159 S Champlain Ave, Chicago, IL 60628
sights.w: The 1890s market square at the centre of George Pullman's company town — once 16 market stalls and a meeting hall, ringed by colonnaded apartments still lived in today; now a public-art site in the national park.

sights.address: Division St / Milwaukee Ave / Ashland Ave, Wicker Park–Noble Square, Chicago
sights.w: The plaza at the heart of old 'Polish Downtown', where nearly every major Polish-American organisation once had its headquarters — summer 'Tuesdays at the Triangle' events.

sights.address: 3100 W 26th St, Chicago, IL 60623
sights.w: Adrian Lozano's 1990 tiled gateway arch — 'Bienvenidos A Little Village' — over 26th Street, the Mexican capital of the Midwest; a Chicago Landmark since 2022, restored 2024.
